approvedMerges.text: Fully satisfy agreed scope without speculative expansion; preserve unrelated work, intended domain/API behavior and stored formats. Ask before consequential expansion or destruction, including rule changes. Update genuinely stale tests for agreed changes, never weaken them to hide regressions. This covers presentation scope without a standalone UI rule. Checking affected API consumers belongs under verification.
For production behavior, run a focused failing test first, implement only enough to pass, then refactor as needed while keeping tests green.

Prefer tests derived from requirements and observable public behavior over private implementation details, with concise representative fixtures preserving tested distinctions rather than copied live records. Justify focused internal-unit tests while preserving meaningful verification and isolation.

After Green, review duplication and prefer cohesive functions; extract meaningful responsibilities/reuse, not coincidental similarity or forced abstractions. This is not an independent completion gate.

Tests must not mutate real files or perform external service I/O. Read-only filesystem access, console logging, test-local memory/DOM and test-runner reports/caches are allowed; test scenarios must not write real application data or contact services. Spies/fake time are allowed in boundary-adapter/mock tests. Detailed mock-first procedure and testability-refactor guidance are separately Should.

Avoid coverage/testability-driven distortions of production code; justify legitimate boundary/testability refactors and demonstrated unreachable-code cleanup. Preserve scope approval and verified behavior.

Before tests, identify real functional boundaries and reuse simple boundary mocks; prefer injected boundaries for consumers and avoid framework-internal interception. Justify necessary interception or alternative procedures while retaining test isolation.

Before completion, verify the requested outcome with relevant tests, appropriate type-check/build and affected consumers; use runtime/UI checks when needed. Report failed/unavailable checks and uncertainty honestly. Surface errors explicitly rather than hide them with silent or success-shaped fallbacks. The 100% coverage target remains a Should default, not part of this Must gate.

Review missing/refinable domain Types and evidence-backed disproportionate complexity when concepts or representations change; ground candidates in meaning, constraints and genuine real examples, and report meaningful findings with alternatives proportionally. Discuss consequential domain names and keep unapproved names provisional, without approval gates for every local implementation name. This is an applicable default, not a completion gate; avoid repetitive empty reports and preserve scope approval.

Keep one authoritative source; derived views must not become independently maintained authorities. Use appropriate runtime validation of external input; interfaces alone do not validate data. Reuse existing validated boundaries rather than revalidate trusted data everywhere. Typed JSON and explicit-interface representation guidance are separately Should.
Prefer explicit interfaces for structured data as representation guidance, not an unconditional gate.
Prefer Typed JSON for structured data and generate Markdown views where appropriate; retain legitimate narrative/native customization Markdown.

Honor opted-in tracking and metrics choices through follow-ups. For opted-in work, record baseline and completion/follow-up evidence, preserve unknowns, and save decisions, open questions and next step before pausing or switching. Asking about new-task choices is separately Should.
For new substantive tasks, ask separately about resumable tracking and metrics when useful unless already specified; honor existing choices without repeated interviews.

Leave changes uncommitted until explicitly requested. Then verify scope, commit only the authorized scope and verify the resulting worktree. Omit the Copilot co-author trailer. Exact-subject approval is separately Should.
After an explicit commit request, present the exact short subject for approval as an applicable default, not an unconditional gate.
Keep @shared runtime-neutral, including transitive dependencies and public exports. Repository layout/command context is informational, not a selected practice; detailed setup remains in README.

For ruleset/versioning work, default to a version pinned to committed content; preserve history and unknown activation dates. Consult the scoped versioning policy when applicable and justify meaningful deviations.

Use interface for grouped records and type for named values/choices; use named alternatives for structured unions. Follow nearby UI conventions and keep feature-specific details local.
